title: Cup product on module cohomology via acyclic resolutions
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], F,G O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and p,q nonnegative integers. Write H^n(X,-) for the right-derived global-sections cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and F\otimes G for the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A computing resolution of F is a nonnegative complex K with a quasi-isomorphism F[0]\to K, an injective resolution F\to I [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and a comparison K\to I extending the augmentation, whose global-sections map induces isomorphisms in every degree. A resolution pairing consists of computing resolutions of F,G,F\otimes G and restriction-compatible O_X-linear bilinear maps K_F^r(V)\times K_G^s(V)\to K_{F\otimes G}^{r+s}(V), obeying the signed total-tensor Leibniz rule [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and extending s\otimes t in degree zero. The usual sheaf cup product H^p(X,F)\times H^q(X,G)\to H^{p+q}(X,F\otimes G) is characterized as the unique Gamma(X,O_X)-bilinear map that, for every such resolution pairing, carries the cohomology classes of two global cocycles to the class of their paired cocycle. The classes are transported via the comparison to I and the canonical injective-resolution identification, not an arbitrary isomorphism. Equivalently, this is the map induced by RGamma(F)\otimes^L RGamma(G)\to RGamma(F\otimes^L G)\to RGamma(F\otimes G); Godement resolutions compute the characterization.
